claude.sample_unit: mammography examinations (EMBED dataset), simulated daily samples
models_evaluated: CUSUM control chart applied to computer-aided breast cancer detection AI

links.outcome: Detection delay and false alarm interval of CUSUM monitoring for simulated abrupt data drift
links.effect: With drift of 1.5 SD, CUSUM detected changes in test negativity rate within an average of 5 days, with ~293 days between false alarms.
links.quote: Our results indicate that, when the magnitude of the drift is 1.5 times the standard deviation of the performance metric, CUSUM is able to detect changes in the test negativity rate of an AI model within an average of 5 days following the onset of performance drift, with a long duration ( ∼ 293 days) between false alarms.

links.outcome: Tuning CUSUM alarm thresholds to balance false alarms against detection delay
links.effect: CUSUM sensitivity can be controlled to balance mean time between false alarms and delay in detecting a true performance change; almost no false alarms in 60 days at 40 samples/day.
links.quote: We demonstrate that the sensitivity of CUSUM can be controlled to balance the mean time between false alarms and the delay in detecting a true change in performance.

links.outcome: CUSUM false alarms and detection delay
links.effect: With 40 samples/day, almost no false alarms were expected in 60 days with small true alarm detection delay.
links.quote: Our results also indicate that when the average number of samples is 40/day, leading to a reasonable standard deviation for the performance metric, almost no false alarms are expected in a period of 60 days, with the choice of CUSUM parameters that lead to a small true alarm detection delay.
